parts.prompt: Directions: Suppose it is proposed that university students should be required to participate in at least one research project. You are now to write a response by stating what you think of the proposal in terms of its necessity and practicality. You will have 30 minutes to write the response. You should write at least 120 words but not more than 180 words.

reference.essayTranslation:
如今，有一份提案称大学生应被要求至少参与一项研究项目。①在我看来，这一提案既有必要又切实可行，理应得到充分的支持。
一方面，研究项目对学生的全面发展至关重要，它们能让学生将理论知识应用于现实问题中，帮助他们加深对专业的理解。此外，参与研究项目有助于培养批判性思维，这正是就业市场高度重视的。另一方面，该提案具有很强的可行性。②大多数高校都配备了专业的导师、图书馆和实验设施，为实施这一提案奠定了坚实的基础。更重要的是，由于国家在各类研究项目上的投入，学生获得了更多参与这些活动的机会。
总的来看，这项提案确实值得落实。③是时候找准我们的优势，打造属于自己的核心竞争力了。
reference.modelEssay:
Nowadays, there is a proposal that university students should be required to participate in at least one research project. ①As far as I am concerned, this proposal is both necessary and practical, and thus deserves full support.
On the one hand, research projects are essential for students' all-round development, which allow students to apply theoretical knowledge to real-world problems, helping them deepen their understanding of majors. Besides, participating in research projects helps cultivate critical thinking highly valued in the job market. On the other hand, the proposal is highly practical. ②Most universities are equipped with professional tutors, libraries and experimental facilities, which lay a solid foundation for implementing this idea. Most importantly, owing to the country's investment in various research projects, more opportunities are provided for students to participate in such activities.
Overall, taking everything into consideration, this proposal is well worth carrying out. ③It is time for us to find our strengths and develop our own superiority.
reference.shenTi: 作文要求围绕“大学生应被要求至少参与一项研究项目”这一校园提案展开论述。首段明确表达对该提案的支持态度。主体段从“必要性”与“可行性”两个维度进行论证：一是聚焦该提案对学生全面发展的价值，论述研究项目能深化学生对专业的理解以及培养批判性思维，以此证明该提案对学生成长的重要意义；二是聚焦实施该提案的现实条件，从学校配置到国家投入两个层面展开叙述，表明该提案具备现实可行性。最后一段重申该提案值得推行的结论，再以呼吁式表达收尾，传递“积极参与”的态度，呼应开头的支持立场，使文章结构更有层次。

items.groupHeader: Questions 1 and 2 are based on the news report you have just heard.

options.textEn: He had bought meals with his online food ordering account.
options.textZhGloss: 他用自己的线上订餐账户买了餐食。

options.textEn: His son had used his cell phone to pay for playing a game.
options.textZhGloss: 他的儿子用他的手机支付了游戏费用。

options.textEn: His son had ordered food from several restaurants.
options.textZhGloss: 他的儿子从多家餐厅订了食物。

options.textEn: He had dined out at a famous five-star restaurant.
options.textZhGloss: 他在一家知名五星级餐厅用餐。

distractors: 干扰项排除 录音中是他的儿子在线上订了食物,而不是他自己,故排除 A)项;录音中表明他儿子付的是食物费用,而非“游戏费用”,故排除 B)项;录音中未提及在五星级餐厅用餐,故排除 D)项。

evidence.location: News Report One
evidence.quote: A man was left with a $1,000 bill, after his 6-year-old son ordered a virtual buffet of food from several restaurants last weekend.

review.explanation: 解析 答案为 C)。句[1]提到,上周末,一名男子6岁的儿子从多家餐厅线上点了一堆食物,导致他收到了一张1000美元的账单。C)项是对录音中 his 6-year-old son ordered a virtual buffet of food from several restaurants 的同义转述,故为答案。
review.questionTranslation: 为什么基思·斯通豪斯会收到一张1000美元的账单?

items.groupHeader: Questions 1 and 2 are based on the news report you have just heard.

options.textEn: Teach his son a lesson.
options.textZhGloss: 给他儿子一个教训。

options.textEn: Change his password.
options.textZhGloss: 更改自己的密码。

options.textEn: Ask his neighbors for help.
options.textZhGloss: 向他的邻居寻求帮助。

options.textEn: Buy a bigger refrigerator.
options.textZhGloss: 买一个更大的冰箱。

distractors: 干扰项排除 A)项在录音中未提及,故排除;C)项是依据录音中的 neighbors 设置的干扰,但录音中说的是邀请一些邻居来吃饭,而不是向邻居寻求帮助,故排除;D)项是依据录音中的 refrigerators 设置的干扰,但录音中提到的是大部分食物都存进了家里的冰箱里,而非要买一个更大的冰箱,故排除。

evidence.location: News Report One
evidence.quote: The father is planning to change his password.

review.explanation: 解析 答案为 B)。句[2]提到,这位父亲打算更改自己的密码。B)项是对录音中 change his password 的原词复现,故为答案。
review.questionTranslation: 新闻报道提到基思·斯通豪斯打算做什么?

items.groupHeader: Questions 3 and 4 are based on the news report you have just heard.

options.textEn: They examined how visitors affected animal behaviour in zoos.
options.textZhGloss: 他们研究了游客如何影响动物园内的动物行为。

options.textEn: They studied when the best time to feed animals in public was.
options.textZhGloss: 他们研究了在公共场合喂养动物的最佳时间。

options.textEn: They studied how animals adapted themselves to life in zoos.
options.textZhGloss: 他们研究了动物如何适应动物园生活。

options.textEn: They examined what behaviours indicated animal boredom.
options.textZhGloss: 他们研究了哪些行为表明动物感到无聊。

distractors: 干扰项排除 录音中仅提到在投喂时段动物行为的变化，并未研究投喂的最佳时间，故排除 B)项；录音仅提到部分动物物种很可能已经习惯了人类的存在，但并未提到专家研究了动物如何适应动物园生活，故排除 C)项；录音仅提到重复性行为通常代表动物无聊，但并未提到专家研究了哪些行为表明动物感到无聊，故排除 D)项。

evidence.location: News Report Two
evidence.quote: They examined how visitors affected the behaviour of more than 250 species in zoos.

review.explanation: 解析 答案为 A)。句[3]提到,他们研究了游客如何影响动物园内 250 多种动物的行为。A)项是对录音中 They examined how visitors affected the behaviour of more than 250 species in zoos 的同义转述,故为答案。
review.questionTranslation: 根据新闻报道,动物行为专家做了什么?

items.groupHeader: Questions 3 and 4 are based on the news report you have just heard.

options.textEn: They socialise with zookeepers as well as with each other.
options.textZhGloss: 它们与动物饲养员以及彼此之间进行社交。

options.textEn: They show good adaptability to living with humans.
options.textZhGloss: 它们对与人类共处表现出良好的适应能力。

options.textEn: They have been kept as pets by humans.
options.textZhGloss: 它们曾被人类作为宠物饲养。

options.textEn: They have been born and raised in zoos.
options.textZhGloss: 它们是在动物园中出生并长大的。

distractors: 干扰项排除 录音仅提到在公众喂食时段,大象之间的社交互动显著增加,但并未提到与动物饲养员进行社交,且这也并非部分动物物种习惯人类存在的原因,故排除 A)项;“良好的适应能力”是动物习惯人类存在的表现,并非其原因,故排除 B)项;录音未提到动物被人类作为宠物饲养,故排除 C)项。

evidence.location: News Report Two
evidence.quote: Some animal species have been born and raised in zoos, and so have likely become used to the presence of humans.

review.explanation: 解析 答案为 D)。句[4]提到,部分动物物种是在动物园中出生并长大的,因此很可能已经习惯了人类的存在。D)项是对录音中 have been born and raised in zoos 的原词复现,故为答案。
review.questionTranslation: 为什么部分动物物种很可能已经习惯了人类的存在?

items.groupHeader: Questions 5 to 7 are based on the news report you have just heard.

options.textEn: Adjusting it.
options.textZhGloss: 调整该项目。

options.textEn: Suspending it.
options.textZhGloss: 暂停该项目。

options.textEn: Reevaluating it.
options.textZhGloss: 重新评估该项目。

options.textEn: Expanding it.
options.textZhGloss: 扩大该项目。

distractors: 干扰项排除 录音提到,市政府随后调整了该项目,限制每月申请人数,周一,市政府宣布暂停该项目,因此调整只是项目暂停前的临时操作,并非丹佛市的核心举措,故排除A)项;C)项和D)项在录音中未提及,故排除。

evidence.location: News Report Three
evidence.quote: Denver is suspending its popular electric bike incentive program.

review.explanation: 解析 答案为 B)。句[5]提到,丹佛市正暂停其深受欢迎的电动自行车激励项目。B)项是对录音中 suspending 的原词复现,故为答案。
review.questionTranslation: 丹佛市对其深受欢迎的电动自行车激励项目采取了什么行动?

items.groupHeader: Questions 5 to 7 are based on the news report you have just heard.

options.textEn: They could buy an electric bike for $400 in April.
options.textZhGloss: 人们可以在四月份花400美元购买一辆电动自行车。

options.textEn: They could buy their first electric bike at a discount.
options.textZhGloss: 人们可以以折扣价购入自己的第一辆电动自行车。

options.textEn: They could enjoy free after-sale service for their purchase.
options.textZhGloss: 人们购买后可以享受免费售后服务。

options.textEn: They could get $1,200 from government funds if they qualified.
options.textZhGloss: 符合条件者可从政府基金中获得1200美元。

distractors: 干扰项排除 400 美元是政府补贴金额,不是电动自行车的售价,且四月份是项目上线的时间,并非指在四月份才能低价买车,故排除 A)项;录音未提到人们可以以折扣价购入自己的第一辆电动自行车或享受免费售后服务,故排除 B)项和 C)项。

evidence.location: News Report Three
evidence.quote: Residents who met certain income qualifications could qualify for $1,200.

review.explanation: 解析 答案为 D)。句[6]提到,符合特定收入条件的居民可申领1200美元补助。D)项是对录音中Residents who met certain income qualifications could qualify for $1,200的同义转述,故为答案。
review.questionTranslation: 电动自行车激励项目是如何造福居民的?

items.groupHeader: Questions 5 to 7 are based on the news report you have just heard.

options.textEn: Put 400 more electric bikes on its streets.
options.textZhGloss: 在街道再投放400辆电动自行车。

options.textEn: Increase the program funding by 8 percent.
options.textZhGloss: 将项目资金增加8%。

options.textEn: Resume its electric bike incentive program.
options.textZhGloss: 恢复其电动自行车激励项目。

options.textEn: Invest millions of dollars into the local economy.
options.textZhGloss: 向当地经济投资数百万美元。

distractors: 干扰项排除 录音仅提到“已经投放了4400辆电动自行车”，但并未提到要“再投放400辆电动自行车”，故排除A)项；B)项在录音中未提及，故排除；录音提到，该计划“已经为当地经济注入860万美元”，但这是往年的成果，而不是明年的计划，故排除D)项。

evidence.location: News Report Three
evidence.quote: The city expects to resume the program early next year.

review.explanation: 解析 答案为 C)。句[7]提到,该市预计将于明年年初恢复该项目。C)项是对录音中 resume the program 的同义转述,故为答案。
review.questionTranslation: 丹佛市预计明年年初要做什么?

items.groupHeader: Questions 8 to 11 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

options.textEn: The coin collection.
options.textZhGloss: 硬币收藏。

options.textEn: The primitive tools.
options.textZhGloss: 原始工具。

options.textEn: The ancient ornaments.
options.textZhGloss: 古代饰品。

options.textEn: The 2,000-year-old clothes.
options.textZhGloss: 有两千年历史的衣物。

distractors: 干扰项排除 录音中男士仅提到原始工具是展品之一，并未提到这是他最喜欢的展品，故排除 B) 项；C) 项在录音中未提及，故排除；录音中提到，有些古钱币已经有两千多年的历史，而不是男士喜欢有两千年历史的衣物，故排除 D) 项。

evidence.location: Conversation One
evidence.quote: but my favorite is the coin collection.

review.explanation: 解析 答案为 A)。句[8]男士提到,但他最喜欢的还是硬币收藏。A)项是对录音中 the coin collection 的原词复现,故为答案。
review.questionTranslation: 男士在参观的博物馆里最喜欢哪些展品?

items.groupHeader: Questions 8 to 11 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

options.textEn: It is charming with narrow but beautiful streets.
options.textZhGloss: 它魅力十足,街道狭窄却很美。

options.textEn: It attracts visitors from every corner of the world.
options.textZhGloss: 它吸引着来自世界各地的游客。

options.textEn: It has flowers displayed around the Trevi Fountain.
options.textZhGloss: 其特雷维喷泉周围摆放着鲜花。

options.textEn: It is more attractive than the pictures in guidebooks.
options.textZhGloss: 它比旅游指南中的图片更吸引人。

distractors: 干扰项排除 录音中仅提到男士和女士都认为老城区游客太多了，但女士并未提到她认为老城区吸引着来自世界各地的游客，故排除 B)项；录音中提到摆放着鲜花的是带有西班牙阶梯的广场，而非特雷维喷泉，C)项与录音内容不符，故排除；录音中并未对比实景和旅游指南中的图片，D)项属于无中生有，故排除。

evidence.location: Conversation One
evidence.quote: The streets are narrow but beautiful with plenty of charm.

review.explanation: 解析 答案为 A)。句[9]女士提到,街道狭窄却美丽,颇具魅力。A)项中的 charming 是对录音中 charm 的同义转述,narrow but beautiful 是原词复现,故为答案。
review.questionTranslation: 关于老城区,女士说了什么?

items.groupHeader: Questions 8 to 11 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

options.textEn: It is covered with wild grass.
options.textZhGloss: 它长满了野草。

options.textEn: It is very famous and pretty.
options.textZhGloss: 它非常著名且十分美丽。

options.textEn: It is located away from an old church.
options.textZhGloss: 它距离一座老教堂很远。

options.textEn: It is surrounded by Spanish-style houses.
options.textZhGloss: 它被西班牙风格的房屋环绕。

distractors: 干扰项排除 A)项和 D)项在录音中未提及,故排除;录音中仅提到广场一侧有宽阔的台阶,可通向教堂,而非广场距离教堂很远,故排除 C)项。

evidence.location: Conversation One
evidence.quote: It's very famous and pretty.

review.explanation: 解析 答案为 B)。句[10]男士提到,它非常著名且十分美丽。B)项是对录音中 It is very famous and pretty 的原词复现,故为答案。
review.questionTranslation: 关于带有西班牙阶梯的广场,男士说了什么?

items.groupHeader: Questions 8 to 11 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

options.textEn: Ask Kathy what her plan is.
options.textZhGloss: 问问凯茜她的计划是什么。

options.textEn: Tell Kathy Mike will join them.
options.textZhGloss: 告诉凯茜迈克会加入她们。

options.textEn: Ask Kathy if she'd like to see the square.
options.textZhGloss: 问问凯茜是否想参观这个广场。

options.textEn: Tell Kathy Mike would like to have a change.
options.textZhGloss: 告诉凯茜迈克想要换个安排。

distractors: 干扰项排除 女士首先要做的是询问凯茜是否想参观这个广场，并非询问凯茜的计划是什么，A)项与录音内容不符，故排除；录音中是女士和凯茜想要加入迈克的行程，并非告知凯茜迈克会加入她们，故排除 B)项；D)项在录音中未提及，故排除。

evidence.location: Conversation One
evidence.quote: Let me ask her first, but I'm sure she'll be up for it.

review.explanation: 解析 答案为 C)。录音中男士提到自己明天打算去参观带有西班牙阶梯的广场，随后女士询问自己与凯茜是否能够同行，并在句[11]表示，要先问问凯茜，但自己相信她一定会同意的。由此可知，女士会先询问凯茜是否想参观这个广场，C)项是对录音内容的同义转述，故为答案。
review.questionTranslation: 女士说她打算首先做什么?

items.groupHeader: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

options.textEn: How to fit into the bigger picture.
options.textZhGloss: 如何融入整体大局。

options.textEn: How to get on with colleagues.
options.textZhGloss: 如何与同事相处。

options.textEn: How to create a solid first impression.
options.textZhGloss: 如何给人留下良好的第一印象。

options.textEn: How to succeed in a new job.
options.textZhGloss: 如何在新工作中取得成功。

distractors: 干扰项排除 A)项“如何融入整体大局”和C)项“如何给人留下良好的第一印象”都是录音中女士提到的细节信息，并非男士想要获取建议的核心出发点，故均排除；B)项在录音中未提及，故排除。

evidence.location: Conversation Two
evidence.quote: Can you give me advice about being successful at a new job?

review.explanation: 解析 答案为 D)。句[12]男士提到,您能给我一些在新工作中取得成功的建议吗? D)项是对录音中 being successful at a new job 的同义转述,故为答案。
review.questionTranslation: 男士想从女士那里得到什么建议?

items.groupHeader: Questions 12 to 15 are based on the conversation you have just heard.

options.textEn: Get familiar with all the details of his job description.
options.textZhGloss: 熟悉其职位描述的全部细节。

options.textEn: Learn about the relations within the organization.
options.textZhGloss: 了解组织内部的关系。

options.textEn: Recognize his own limitations and weaknesses.
options.textZhGloss: 认识自身的局限性和弱点。

options.textEn: Understand his role from various perspectives.
options.textZhGloss: 从多个角度理解他的职责。

distractors: 干扰项排除 录音中女士提到,你在工作中的任务并不仅限于职位描述中所列出的职责,故排除 A)项;录音中女士提到男士要思考自己的工作如何与组织内的其他成员产生关联,而不是了解组织内部的关系,故排除 B)项;C)项在录音中未提及,故排除。

banked_cloze.fullTextTranslation:
工业革命最大的争议是它如何影响了工人阶级。最早的争论集中在生活水平是上升还是下降。认为生活水平下降的一方声称，资本家从工人阶级身上[26]榨取了每一盎司能获得的剩余价值；而认为生活水平提高的一方则指出，当时的社会环境对消费者有利，工人阶级每年都[27]能获得越来越多的商品。

如今的历史学家普遍认为，总体而言，生活水平[28]提高了。但他们对于这种提高究竟[29]发生在何时仍存在分歧。

为了解决这一争议，历史学家试图[30]准确界定“生活水平”的含义。他们似乎都同意这应指幸福感，但幸福感却无法衡量。因此，历史学家[31]通常以“实际收入”作为衡量生活水平的指标。实际收入是指扣除生活成本后的实际[32]所得。然而，这种方法并未考虑失业、污染、健康状况、预期寿命以及闲暇时间等因素。

在对平均收入进行了[33]令人疲惫不堪的讨论和分析后，历史学家就工业革命期间经济增长是快速还是缓慢的问题无法达成共识。但他们决定[34]说明工业革命是如何受到其他事件影响的。他们认为，工业革命总体上产生了积极[35]影响，但这可能被战争、高税收以及人口快速增长等负面因素所抵消。

[47]科学无法对“有机食品是否‘更好’”这个问题给出明确答案。这其中往往存在权衡取舍，答案会根据所考虑的产品而变得不那么确定。

有一点是确定的：有机种植与传统种植的食品营养成分相当。从营养学角度来看，有机产品与传统种植的产品并无差异。

有机食品的杀虫剂未必更少——事实上，它们可能更多。[48]从食品安全角度来看，有机与非有机食品也没有明显差别。即便是有机种植者也会使用杀虫剂。检测显示，传统种植食品上的杀虫剂残留即便有也微乎其微。

事实上，有机农民往往会使用更多的杀虫剂，因为他们只能使用天然杀虫剂。化学杀虫剂的杀虫范围通常比任何一种天然杀虫剂都要广得多。

有机农业中动物粪便的使用，也可能成为大肠杆菌、沙门氏菌等细菌传播的诱因。在过去十年里，按比例计算，加拿大有机食品的食品安全召回事件比传统食品更多。

information_matching.fullTextTranslation:
新西兰大巴里尔岛的星空品质

A) 我很庆幸自己患上了如此严重的时差反应。[40]凌晨3:30，状态完全清醒，我和我们9岁的女儿一起在住所的阳台上，凝视了数小时我此生见过的最令人难以置信的夜空，直到黎明开始慢慢抹去地平线上的星星，多颗流星也逐渐消失。

B) 我们原本是要去新西兰奥克兰参加我妻子盛大的家族聚会，[43]但当我们发现就在海岸附近的大巴里尔岛最近获得了“国际暗夜保护区”认证——一个通常偏远、拥有“非凡或卓越的星空夜景”的地区——我们认为这将是我们在繁忙行程开始前放松身心的完美之地。它是全球第一个获此认证的岛屿，也是全球仅有的第四个获此认证的地方。

C) [36-1]带着两个晕机的孩子，经历了28小时的飞行，当我们看到那架将载着我们跨越90千米、从豪拉基湾前往大巴里尔岛的小型双引擎10座飞机时，我们的心沉了下去。但我们本不必担心的。无论是飞机爬升时的重力作用还是引擎的噪音，[36-2]都让我们三岁的女儿立刻入睡，直到我们在克拉里斯机场的草地上颠簸着陆。出乎意料的是，我们第一个呕吐袋竟然完全没用上……情况开始好转了。
D) [44] 大巴里尔岛没有公共设施，住在那里的950人（虽然只有大约一半是永久居民）依靠太阳能和风能，以及瓶装煤气做饭。这里没有路灯。也没有自动取款机或银行。警察部队是由一对夫妇组成的，而这里只有一位邮递员。在这个独特而迷人的景点，令人愉悦的不仅是没有光污染，也没有噪音。大约700年前，东波利尼西亚人首次发现了这座岛屿，毛利人将这座岛命名为奥蒂亚。库克船长给了这座岛它的欧洲名字，因为它在太平洋和豪拉基湾之间起到了屏障的作用。

E) 这里的气候和奥克兰一样是亚热带气候。这座岛拥有一片美丽的荒野，有茂密的森林、壮丽而未经破坏的沙滩，以及众多的海湾和几处山区，在那边湿地和山谷之间有很好的步行道。你可以观鸟、潜水、冲浪和划船。最好的海滩在岛的东侧，那里冲浪也更好些。背风的西侧是你可以找到的最佳潜水和划船的地方。[38]许多人来这里是为了岛周围绝佳的钓鱼点。像新西兰的许多地方一样，这里有观鲸之旅，而且你可能会看到鲨鱼。

F) 很难找到一个真正让人感觉未被发现的岛屿——但这里就是。当我妻子的一个经常来这里的亲戚发现我们去过后，他半开玩笑地压低声音对我们说：“嘘——别告诉任何人！”当地人随性、友善——他们中的许多人告诉我们，[41]这里就像怀赫科岛（现在实际上是奥克兰的一个郊区）在1970年代时的样子，那时它是一个艺术家和想要逃离城市的人聚居的地方。

G) 停留期间，我们的向导是令人钦佩的希尔德·霍文，一位暗夜协会的大使，她与黛博拉·基尔加伦和奥拉·库米斯基一起经营观星旅游公司 Good Heavens。他们把道布森望远镜和豆袋软椅（睁大眼睛凝望天空而没有颈部支撑是很累的事儿）带到岛上的任何地方，还有热巧克力，大女儿听说这点后十分开心。[45]“很奇怪，但当进行光读数时，”希尔德说，她解释这座岛是如何获得其特殊地位的，“他们发现北面来自大约3000千米外的斐济的光污染比南面来自奥克兰的还要多。这里相当暗！”

H) 希尔德和奥拉用绿色激光笔开始了他们的天文幻灯片演示，向我们展示了有白矮星的M4球状星团、土星及土星环、南十字座和横贯天空的银河。我们的女儿对希尔德讲述的毛利神话——用毛伊的鱼钩来解释天蝎座的形状——特别着迷。在这个神话中，半神英雄毛伊用他的鱼钩从海底钓起了新西兰北岛。

I) [37] 我们住在圣保罗山庄园，友善的加拿大夫妇克里斯和蒂拉经营着这家豪华旅馆。蒂拉曾是奥克兰朗廷酒店的厨师，所以围着一张巨大的圆桌（由世界上最古老的树木之一制成）享用的晚餐，正如你所期望的那样令人垂涎欲滴。在俯瞰未经破坏的白色沙滩的阳台上吃薄饼，是开始一天的美好方式。

J) [42]另一个亮点是步行一小时前往岛中心的凯多可温泉，穿过湿地和森林，我们在那里惬意地消磨了整整一个小时，坐在池子里，池子上方层层精致的伞状植物可以遮挡炎热。

K) 我们也很喜欢拜访陶艺家莎拉·哈里森，她带我们参观了她在肖尔湾港口的工作室，以及她的许多罐子、壶、盘子和碗，还有色彩缤纷的马赛克。在她的作品中，她还使用了许多在海滩上找到的材料。我们的大女儿喜欢梅德兰兹海滩那个迷人的隐蔽水池，那里的水在一个私密的岩石池中与大海分隔开来。其他亮点包括古老的波胡图卡瓦树，以及从风峡谷顶部俯瞰奥基维盆地和旺加普阿海滩的令人难以置信的景色，只需步行10分钟，穿过狭窄的山谷，沿着岛东侧一些陡峭的木质台阶上去即可。

L) [39]据说，岛议会拒绝了著名音乐家保罗·麦卡特尼购买大巴里尔岛房产的申请，因为他会带来那种不受欢迎的关注。你可以明白他为什么想来这里；同样，这座岛也非常清楚它更喜欢哪种观星方式。

paragraphs.text: I was glad I had such terrible jetlag. Wide awake at 3:30am with our nine-year-old daughter on our lodge balcony, I stared for hours at the most incredible night sky I've ever seen before the dawn slowly started to rub out the stars on the horizon and the multiple shooting stars faded away.

We were going to my wife's big family reunion in Auckland, New Zealand, but when we found out that Great Barrier Island, just off the coast, had been recently awarded Dark Sky Sanctuary status—a typically remote area that has an "exceptional or distinguished quality of starry nights"—we thought it would be the perfect place to relax before our busy schedule. It's the first island and only the fourth location in the world to achieve this status.

After a 28-hour flight with two travel-sick children, our hearts sank when we saw the tiny twin engine 10-seater that was to take us the 90km across the Hauraki Gulf to Great Barrier Island. But we needn't have worried. Whether it was the gravity force of the plane climbing or the noise of the engine, it put our three-year-old daughter instantly to sleep until we bumped down on the grass at Claris Airport. Our first empty sick bag against all the odds...Things were looking up.

Great Barrier Island has no public facilities and the 950 people living there (though only about half permanently) rely on solar and wind energy, and bottled gas for cooking. There are no streetlights. There are no cash machines or banks. The police force comprises a husband and wife, and there's one postman. It's not just the lack of light but the lack of noise that's so delightful on this unique and gorgeous scene. It was first discovered by East Polynesians about 700 years ago and the Maori name for the island is Aotea. Captain Cook gave the island its European name, because it acts as a barrier between the Pacific and the Hauraki Gulf.

The climate here is subtropical (亚热带的) like Auckland's. The island boasts a beautiful wilderness with dense forests, glorious, unspoilt sandy beaches and plenty of bays and a few mountainous areas where there are good walking tracks among the wetlands and valleys. You can birdwatch, dive, surf and boat. The best beaches are on the eastern side of the island where the surf is better, too. The sheltered western side is where you'll find the best diving and boating. Lots of people come here for the fantastic fishing spots around the island. Like a lot of spots in New Zealand, there are whale-watching trips and you might just catch sight of sharks.

It's rare to find an island that really does feel undiscovered—but this is it. When one of my wife's relations, who comes here regularly, found out that we'd been there, he whispered to us, only half-joking: "Shh—don't tell anyone!" The locals are a relaxed and friendly bunch—a lot of them told us that it's like what Waiheke Island (now in effect a suburb of Auckland) was in the 1970s when it was a commune of artists and people wanting to escape the city.

Our guide for some of our stay was the inestimable Hilde Hoven, a Dark Sky ambassador who runs Good Heavens with Deborah Kilgallon and Orla Cumisky. They bring their Dobsonian telescope and beanbags (it's hard work staring up wide-eyed in wonder without neck support) and, our elder daughter was glad to hear, hot chocolate to wherever you are on the island. "It's odd but when the light readings were done," said Hilde, explaining how the island was awarded its special status, "they found there was more light pollution on the northern side coming from Fiji, which is about 3,000km away, than Auckland to the south. It's pretty dark!"

Beginning their astronomical PowerPoint demonstration using a green laser pointer, Hilde and Orla showed us the Messier 4 spherical cluster (星团) with white dwarf stars (白矮星), Saturn and its rings, the Southern Cross and the Milky Way, which stretched across the sky. Our daughter was especially taken with Hilde's narrating of the Maori myth of Māui's fish hook to explain the shape of Scorpius. In the fable, Māui hauled the North Island of New Zealand from the bottom of the ocean with his hook.

We stayed at Mount St Paul's Estate, a luxurious lodge run by the friendly Chris and Teara, both from Canada. Teara used to be a chef at the Langham in Auckland and so dinner, eaten around a huge circular table (made of one of the most ancient trees in the world), was every bit as mouth-watering as you'd expect. Eating pancakes on the balcony overlooking the unspoilt white sandy beach was a great way to start the day.

Another highlight was an hour-long walk to Kaitoke hot pools in the centre of the island, through wetlands and a forest, where we whiled away a good hour sitting in the pools shaded from the heat by layers of delicate umbrella-like plants.

We also loved visiting the potter (陶艺家) Sarah Harrison, who showed us round her studio at Shoal Bay harbour, and her many pots and jugs, plates and bowls and colourful mosaics (马赛克). In her work, she also uses a lot of materials found on the beach. Our elder daughter loved the gorgeous hidden pool at Medlands beach where the water is separated from the sea in a private rock pool. Other high points were the ancient pohutukawa trees and the incredible views of Okiwi Basin and Whangapoua beach from the top of Windy Canyon, just a 10-minute hike through a narrow valley up some steep wooden steps on the eastern side of the island.

Apparently the island council turned down famous musician Paul McCartney's application to buy a property at Great Barrier Island because of the unwelcome attention he would have brought. You can see why he wanted to come here; equally, the island knows exactly what kind of star watching it prefers.

blocks.text: Is organic food worth the higher price? It's the classic grocery store dilemma. On the one hand, your family dinner table deserves only the best. On the other hand, your wallet can only stretch so far.
Whether or not to buy organic is a personal decision, said Mike von Massow, professor of Food Agriculture.

Science won't give a clear-cut answer to the question of whether organic food is "better." There are often trade-offs (权衡) and answers become less definitive depending on the product under consideration.
One thing is definitive: Organic and conventionally grown food are equally nutritious. From a nutrition point of view, there is no difference between organic and traditionally grown products.

Organic products don't necessarily have fewer pesticides (杀虫剂)—in fact, they may have more. There is also no big difference between organic and non-organic products from a food-safety perspective. Even organic growers use pesticides. Testing shows little if any pesticide remains on conventionally grown products.

In fact, organic farmers often use larger quantities of pesticide because they can only use the natural variety of insect-killers. Chemical pesticides generally kill a much wider range of pests (害虫) than any single natural pesticide.

The use of animal waste in organic agriculture can also be a factor in the spread of bacteria like E. coli and salmonella. Over the past 10 years, Canada has seen more food-safety recalls for organic products, proportionally, than for conventional products.

On the whole, organic agriculture may have a smaller environmental footprint. That's mostly because the risk of groundwater contamination from organic farming is lower. Organic farmers never used neonics, the controversial pesticides that have been linked to shrinking bee populations worldwide.
Traditional agriculture has been making "dramatic improvements" to reduce its impact on the environment.
It isn't a black-and-white picture, though.
Organic farming is much less efficient when it comes to land use, although yields vary considerably depending on the crop.

On the other hand, advocates of organic farming argue yields and efficiency could be significantly improved if the food industry devoted as much research and money to organic farming as it does conventional agriculture

items.stemEn: What can we infer from the last paragraph?

blocks.text: It is still controversial whether we are fundamentally generous or selfish and whether these tendencies are shaped by our genes or environment.
Some evidence points to humans being born cooperative. At later stages in life we routinely work together to reach goals and help out in times of need.

Yet instances of selfish behavior are also plenty. One recent study tested people's willingness to set aside selfish interests to reach a greater good. It found that being selfish was more advantageous than cooperating. The benefit may be short-lived, however. Another study showed that players who cooperated did better in the long run.

It seems that human nature supports both pro-social and selfish traits (特征). Genetic studies have made some progress toward identifying their biological roots. By comparing identical twins, who share nearly 100 percent of their genes, and non-identical twins, who share about half, researchers have found overwhelming evidence for genetic effects on behaviors. In these twin studies, identical and non-identical twins are asked, for example, to split a sum of money with a peer. Such studies often also rely on careful psychological assessments and DNA analysis.

Other work highlights specific genes as key players. My colleagues and I recently identified a gene linked to altruistic (利他的) behavior and found that a particular variant of it was associated with more selfish behavior in preschoolers.

According to evolutionary scientists, cooperative behavior may have evolved first among relatives to promote the continuation of their genetic line. As communities diversified, mutual support could have broadened to include individuals not linked by blood. Another possibility is that humans cooperate to gain some advantage, such as boosting reputation. Finally, evolutionary processes take place at the group level. Groups of highly cooperative individuals have higher chances of survival because they can work together to reach goals that are unattainable to less cooperative groups.

Yet almost no behavior is entirely genetic, even among identical twins. Culture, schooling and parenting are important determinants of cooperation. Thus, the degree to which we act cooperatively or selfishly is unique to each individual and depends on a variety of genetic and environmental influences.

reference.commentary:
1. 中国有句老话：“一日为师，终身为父”。

句意分析 本句描述的是普遍认可的真理，在英语中，表达谚语、科学事实或普遍真理时，通常使用一般现在时。中文原句无被动含义，因此译文使用主动语态。句子结构较为简单，顺译即可。
“中国有句老话”可译为 As an old Chinese saying goes 或 There is an old saying in China; “一日为师,终身为父”是本句的翻译难点,该谚语的含义为“只教过自己一天的老师,也要一辈子当作父亲看待”,可简译为 A teacher for a day is a father for a lifetime,也可以遵照其含义,译为 One who teaches you, even for a single day, deserves the lifelong respect you give your own father。

2. 在中国人的观念里，老师不仅传授知识，更教给学生做人的道理。

句意分析 本句描述的是普遍观念，属于客观表达，因此译文使用一般现在时。主语“老师”是动作（传授、教给）的执行者，因此译文使用主动语态。“在中国人的观念里”处理为介词短语作状语，置于句首。“不仅……更……”使用“not only... but also...”结构。本句顺译即可。

关键词推敲 “在……的观念里”可译为 In the mindset/eyes/conception/perception of...；“传授知识”可译为 impart knowledge 或 pass on knowledge；“教给学生做人的道理”中的“做人”不可直接译为 being a human，在该句语境中，“做人”是指在社会、伦理、道德层面成为一个合格、得体、有修养的人。“道理”则指其中的准则、原则和智慧。因此“教给学生做人的道理”可译为 teaches students the principles of being a good person。

3. 在古代，学生初次见老师时要举行隆重的仪式，足见老师地位之高。

句意分析 本句可拆分为两个逻辑层次。一是事实描述：在古代，学生初次见老师时要举行隆重的仪式；二是结论评述：足见老师地位之高。在翻译时，可将事实描述“在古代，……仪式”作为主句，结论评述“足见老师地位之高”处理成 which 引导的非限制性定语从句，which 指代前面的事实描述。由“在古代”“初次”可知，主句的翻译需使用一般过去时，且主语“学生”是动作“见”“举行”的执行者，因此主句使用主动语态。“老师地位之高”并非仅指古代那种仪式下的短暂现象，而是一种普遍的社会观念和认知。即使在今天，我们谈论古代的事情，依然可以认为“尊敬老师、老师地位高”是一种跨时代的普遍道理，因此 which 引导的非限制性定语从句需使用一般现在时。

关键词推敲 “在古代”可译为 In ancient times 或 In olden times; “举行”译为 hold 即可; “隆重的仪式”可译为 a solemn/grand/formal ceremony; “足见”可以理解为“完全可以看出/足以说明”, 译为 fully show/reflect/indicate/demonstrate; “老师地位之高”可译为 the high status of teachers, 也可以理解为“老师的地位是多么的高”, 翻译成含有感叹语气的表达, 即 how high teachers' status is。

4. 为弘扬尊师的优良传统，中国从1985年开始将每年的9月10日定为教师节。

句意分析 由“从1985年开始”可知，动作从1985年开始，一直持续到现在，且可能继续下去，因此译文使用现在完成时更合适。如果用一般过去时，只表示“1985年那年定下了”，无法体现“从1985年开始一直延续到现在”的状态。主语“中国”是动作“定为”的执行者，因此译文使用主动语态。“为弘扬尊师的优良传统”是后续动作的目的，因此处理为不定式短语作目的状语，置于句首。“中国从……教师节”作为主句，“从1985年开始”为时间状语，置于句尾，其余成分顺译即可。在本句的译文最开头可加表示因果关系的逻辑关系词Therefore，使本句与第3句衔接更加紧密，清晰地表明，基于古代尊师的事实，所以现代采取了设立教师节的举措。

关键词推敲 “为……”可译为 To do... 或 In order to do...；“……的优良传统”可译为 the fine tradition of...；“尊师”即“尊重老师”，译为 respect teachers；“从……（时间）开始”译为“since+时间点”；“将……定为……”可译为 designate... as... 或 establish... as... 或 set... as...；“教师节”有固定的英文表达，即 Teachers' Day。

5. 在这一天，学生以各种方式表达对老师的敬意。

句意分析 本句描述一个反复发生的规律性行为，即每年的教师节都是如此，因此译文使用一般现在时。主语“学生”是动作“表达”的执行者，因此译文使用主动语态即可。本句为简单句，译文可处理为“时间状语+主谓宾+方式状语”的结构。“在这一天”处理成介词短语作时间状语，置于句首；“学生”为主语；“表达”为谓语；“对老师的敬意”为宾语；“以各种方式”处理成介词短语作方式状语，置于句尾。

关键词推敲 “在这一天”译为 On this day 即可；“以各种方式”可译为 in various/different ways 或 in a variety of ways；“表达对某人的敬意”可译为 express/show respect for sb.。
本句拆分为两个逻辑层次。一是主信息陈述核心事实：尊师是中华民族的传统美德；二是补充信息进一步解释说明核心事实：在当今社会得到了发扬光大。因此，可将主信息“尊师是……美德”作为主句，翻译成“主系表”结构。将补充信息“在当今社会得到了发扬光大”处理成 which 引导的非限制性定语从句，补充说明尊师这一传统美德在当今社会的发展情况。主句描述的是普遍事实，因此译文使用一般现在时。而 which 引导的非限制性定语从句强调从过去到现在这一美德得以延续和发展，且对当下有影响，因此该部分使用现在完成时更合适；“得到发扬光大”隐含“被（社会/人们）发扬光大”的含义，因此该部分需使用被动语态。

关键词推敲 “中华民族”译为 the Chinese nation;“传统美德”可译为 traditional virtue;“得到了发扬光大”应理解为“(尊师这一传统美德)不仅保留下来了,而且做得更好、影响更大”,因此该表达包含两层含义,可译为 be carried forward and greatly enhanced。
reference.referenceEn: As an old Chinese saying goes, “A teacher for a day is a father for a lifetime.” In the mindset of Chinese people, a teacher not only imparts knowledge but also teaches students the principles of being a good person. In ancient times, students held a solemn ceremony when they first met their teachers, which fully shows the high status of teachers. Therefore, to promote the fine tradition of respecting teachers, China has designated September 10th as Teachers' Day since 1985. On this day, students express their respect for their teachers in various ways. Respecting teachers is a traditional virtue of the Chinese nation, which has been carried forward and greatly enhanced in today's society.
